description: [narrowed from narrowing-a-chronically-stuck-gap-copies-it-verbatim-and-only-resets-the-penalty] The chronic-failure narrowing path at gap-to-feature.ts:1988-2014 does not narrow anything. Its own comment states 'The child carries a tighter description and resets failed_attempts to 0'. The code delivers only the second half. The child summary is built as `[narrowed from ${parentId}] ${parentSummary.replace(/^\[narrowed from [\w:.!-]+\]\s*/g, "")}` — the parent summary copied VERBATIM with any prior prefix stripped and a new one prepended. category, source, detected_at, edit_site, and matched_excerpt are all copied unchanged. Verified live: calibration-counts-killswitch-invocations-as-authoring-failures-narrowed is byte-identical to its parent apart from the prefix. THREE CONSEQUENCES. (1) The composer is handed the exact description that already failed three times, so it fails the same way — narrowing cannot relieve chronic failure because nothing was made tighter. This matters most on large files, where the observed failure mode is authoring degradation (the drafter locates the anchor correctly and then emits comment-only content, hard-failed by the semantic gate as zero behaviour delta); a genuinely narrowed scope is exactly the remedy that would help, and it is the one thing not delivered. (2) It is a duplicate mint (law 3): a fresh uninformed row that splits selection traffic and adds nothing to the parent's posterior. (3) Because childMeta sets failed_attempts to 0, the duplicate outranks its own parent, which by then carries a failure penalty. The pair then alternates at the top of the pool indefinitely. This is the mechanism behind the observed thrash: route-edit-db8bd146 / route-edit-db8bd146-narrowed and recommit-route-edit-9077062c-typecheck_dangling_reference-narrowed cycled through essentially every pick for 12+ hours on two underlying targets. FIX: either genuinely narrow the child (derive a tighter scope from the parent's accumulated failure_lessons — the failure classes are already recorded on the gap and would name what to cut), or stop emitting a child and reset the parent's failed_attempts in place, which delivers the only effect the current code actually has without duplicating the row. NOTE: this is the second place in this file where the implementation contradicts its own comment; hopeless() likewise documents 'penalty, not hard exclusion' with 'a re-test path if nothing better exists' and implements a hard continue with no re-test path. A comment that describes intent the code never had is a systematic hazard here, not an isolated slip.
